I calculated the Q3 figures and saved them to `/work/answer.json`. To check the method, I ran the same code on Q2 first and it reproduced all 10 of your reference values exactly.

**Q3 results**

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | `consumer`, 319,684,092 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 246 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | `acc`, 273,911,470 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | `2025-08` |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | `u133@ex.com` |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 235 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 678,199 |
| h. August → September growth | -2.7% |

For reference, the monthly net sales were: July 274,478,943, August 284,688,108 and September 277,053,054. The other segments came to smb 299,187,881 and enterprise 217,348,132.

The data had a few problems that your definitions don't cover. These are the choices that reproduced Q2:
- **Time zone:** order times are stored in UTC (ending in `Z`). Dates and months were only correct after converting to Korean time (UTC+9). So an order at 15:00 UTC or later on 9/30 counts as October and is left out of Q3.
- **Who counts as one customer:** there are 300 customer rows but only 250 distinct emails. Counting customers by email (lowercased, spaces trimmed) gave the Q2 figures for b, e and f. Counting by row id did not.
- **Segment names:** they mix capitals and stray spaces (`' consumer'`, `'Enterprise '`, `'SMB'`), so I trimmed and lowercased them before grouping.
- **Q2 had only two months of data:** the data starts on 2025-05-01. So I took "second month" and "third month" to mean the second and third calendar months of the quarter, not the second and third months that have data.

STATUS: DONE
